subject: Operational slack allowance & monthly remedy cap — proposal
messages:
From: Alex Wong <alex.wong@acmesys.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmesys.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational slack allowance and monthly remedy cap — initial ask

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we scope the contract for production, there are two items Acme needs visibility on before we can proceed to procurement signoff: an allowance for predictable monthly "operational slack" tied to our nightly bulk ingestion window, and a hard monthly remedy cap that keeps our financial exposure bounded.

High level ask:
- Operational slack allowance: carve out up to 120 minutes/month where scheduled heavy batch traffic (we run a nightly 2-hour ingest) may increase P95 latency beyond the standard SLA without triggering full remedy calculations.
- Monthly remedy cap: for any SLA breaches outside the operational slack allowance, Acme requests a remedy cap of 10% of monthly invoice for the first 12 months (pilot).

Rationale: our platform has one short, high-throughput window every night where latency profiles are deliberately bursty. We need to make sure that predictable scheduled load isn’t treated the same as unplanned outages. We are happy to provide the batch schedule (attached) and adjust our ingest timing if Redwood needs it.

Attachments: acme-schedule-batch-windows.csv, acme-operational-slack-request.pdf

Would Redwood consider including a short clause in the SLA that defines the allowed monthly operational slack (minutes and conditions) and a fixed remedy cap for the pilot period? If so, procurement can draft the PO and we can move to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Alex Wong
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Systems
[attachment: acme-schedule-batch-windows.csv (CSV)]
[attachment: acme-operational-slack-request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@acmesys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational slack allowance and monthly remedy cap — initial ask

Alex — thanks for laying this out clearly and for the schedule. I looped in Laura (legal) and Marissa (product ops) to scope practical language and risk. Quick thoughts from the account side:

- We can define an "Operational Slack Allowance" that excludes a bounded number of minutes from monthly uptime/latency calculations so long as those windows are pre-declared and limited (your CSV is helpful).
- For the remedy cap, Redwood is comfortable with a pilot structure, but we need to balance exposure vs. ops incentives. Suggestion: a 15% of monthly invoice cap for the first 3 billing cycles (trial), then revert to 8% steady-state thereafter. This gives Acme protection while aligning incentives to optimize the ingestion pattern.
- Latency carveout granularity: we propose that the allowance applies when p95 latency exceeds the SLA threshold for sustained periods of at least 10 consecutive minutes during a declared batch window. Short spikes under 10 minutes still count toward remedies.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to propose operational rules (how windows are declared, how emergency reschedules are handled).
2) Laura to circulate redline language for the SLA addendum that codifies the allowance and the two-tier remedy cap.
3) If acceptable, we’ll ship a DocuSign amendment for the pilot and have procurement issue a PO.

We’ll keep telemetry and postmortems part of the arrangement so we can refine the allowance if we see systematic issues.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@acmesys.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmesys.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational slack allowance and monthly remedy cap — redline proposal

Hi Alex — appreciate the clear framing. Attached is a redline of the SLA with suggested language. Summary of our proposed changes (redline attached: redwood-sla-amendment-redline.docx):

1) Operational Slack Allowance (section S.3.a):
- Definition: up to 120 minutes per calendar month of pre-declared batch windows ("Declared Batch Window") during which p95 latency may exceed the latency SLO without counting toward monetary remedy calculations.
- Conditions: Acme must publish the monthly schedule at least 7 days in advance; emergency reschedules allowed with 48-hour notice and require joint ops review.

2) Remedy Cap (section S.4.c):
- Pilot period: for the first three invoices after go-live, the maximum monthly remedy payable by Redwood for SLA violations (excluding declared slack) shall be 15% of the monthly invoice.
- Steady-state cap: thereafter remedy shall be capped at 8% of the monthly invoice.
- Remedies are calculated pro rata based on minutes of sustained breach (sustained = >10 consecutive minutes).

3) Latency carveout: explicit note that transient spikes under 10 minutes remain subject to normal remedy calculations.

4) Reporting and escalation: automated telemetry export and a joint weekly runbook review during the pilot.

Attachment: redwood-sla-amendment-redline.docx (redline shows exact language and cross-references). We recommend keeping the pilot to three billing cycles so both teams can evaluate whether the allowance is working as designed. If Acme wants a longer pilot, we'll need to escalate for Exec approval.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-sla-amendment-redline.docx (DOCX)]

From: Alex Wong <alex.wong@acmesys.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmesys.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational slack allowance and monthly remedy cap — agreement in principle

Hi Laura, Sean — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear redline. Acme is fine with the three-invoice pilot at 15% and moving to 8% thereafter, as long as the Declared Batch Window requirement is flexible enough for occasional business-driven reschedules. The 48-hour emergency reschedule notice is acceptable.

Two small asks to finalize before procurement routes the PO:
1) Can you make the pilot period language explicitly tied to "first three invoices after go-live date" (we want to avoid ambiguity if invoices shift).
2) Please include a one-line clarification that remedies under the cap are the exclusive monetary remedy (so we avoid alternate calculators).

If you can update the redline with those two points, procurement will attach the redline to the PO and we’ll route DocuSign. Appreciate the pragmatic approach here — this helps Acme get predictable cost exposure while leaving room to tune.

I’ll await the updated doc and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Systems
